title: The Experience, Captured
objective: Experience the arts event or exhibition through the route in use, and capture the moments on the frame you built, one row at a time, while it is still in front of you.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Week 5. Trinity Arts Award Bronze. The Experience, Captured.
Objective: experience the arts event or exhibition through the route in use, and capture the moments on the frame you built.
Success evidence: four full rows on your frame sheet, each row marked start, middle or end, with one row ringed.

Everything you capture comes from the work in front of you, or from a card in the approved pack. You write about the work: colour, scale, material, sound. You are never asked about your home, your family, your body, how you look or what you believe. Nobody in this room is asked what they believe. Identity here means what you as a maker keep choosing, read off artwork and never off a life.

Nothing is booked. No event and no place is named in this deck. We may go to them. They may come to us. We may meet live on a screen. An online exhibition counts as well. The frame works the same under all three.
40 minutes. Paper and a pencil are all you need to capture.

This deck evidences Bronze Part B, Explore the arts as an audience member. The register says Part B requires attending at least one arts event or experience, reflecting on quality and creative impact, and views shared with at least one other person, evidenced. The register also notes that an online exhibition is legitimate. Nothing is booked: the event comes from EVENT_SLOT, which is UNCONFIRMED, and no venue, organisation, practitioner or date is named anywhere in this deck. It runs unchanged under R1 pupils visit, R2 they come in, and R3 a live remote exchange. Where the experience has not yet run, a card from the approved pack stands in and the rows are labelled preparation, because the slots file counts desk research, archive and video as preparation only. Bronze attempted rule, in the register's words: ONE Attempted allowed overall. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The evidence file cap is 10 evidence files for the whole Bronze level, so today's frame sheet joins the Part B file rather than opening a new one. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Last week's frame sheets out on desks before pupils sit, with one pencil and something hard to lean on. A pupil hunting for a sheet captures nothing.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil has no frame sheet, give them a blank one and let them rule four boxes in the first minute. Do not send anybody out to look for the old one.

blocks.text: Your frame is already built
Last week you built the review frame.
It has four boxes in one row.
Box one is the moment you picked.
Box two is the craft choice you can point at.
Box three is the effect it had on you.
Box four is who the maker made it for.
Today you fill that frame from the work itself.
The work reaches you through the route in use.
The frame does not change with the route.
You need your frame sheet, one pencil and a hard board.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Tell both halves yourself. Do not ask a pupil to model the one who wrote nothing.

blocks.text: What is left an hour later
Two people go through the same experience.
Both look hard. Both like it.
The first writes nothing while it runs.
They tell themselves they will remember it all.
The second fills one row each time something lands.
An hour later, ask them both.
The first has three words: it was good.
The second has four rows, with choices and effects.
The work was the same for both of them.
Only one of them can write a review.

items: Memory keeps the feeling and drops the detail.
The detail is the part a review is built on.
A row written at the time keeps both.

blocks.text: So you capture while it happens, not after.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Model on your own sheet where the group can see it, and fill the four boxes in order without skipping one.
stages.data-ta2: Keep your own row short, about two lines a box. Pupils copy the size of what you write, not the style of it.

blocks.text: I fill one row, out loud
Watch me capture one moment.
I am using a card from the approved pack.
Under the route in use it may be a room, or a screen.
Step one is stop. One moment only.
Something lands, so I stay with it.
Step two is fill. I take the boxes in order.
The moment is the tall grey print at the end.
The craft choice is the ink, thin at the top.
The effect is that my eye ran up and off.
It was made for somebody standing close, not far back.

blocks.caption: Four steps make one row, and then it starts again
blocks.title: The capture loop
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined left to right by arrows, each with a step name in capitals above one line of small text

blocks.text: Step three is mark. I write M in the corner.
M means the moment came in the middle.
Start, middle and end are the three marks.
Step four is move. I leave the row alone.
A row I keep tidying is a row I cannot add to.
Watch the words I did not use.
I did not write nice, boring or amazing.
Those words give a reader nothing to check.
Say the four step names out loud as you do them: stop, fill, mark, move. The loop is the thing being taught here, not the card in your hand.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Cards stay face down until the table is quiet. Turn them over together, then start the clock.

blocks.text: Sort the cards, then match the box
Six cards are on your table. Each card holds one line.

items: The tall grey print at the end.
It was a really good one.
The ink is thin at the top.
My eye ran up and off the paper.
It was made for somebody standing close.
I liked the artist a lot.

blocks.text: Sort them into two piles: goes on the frame, and does not.
A frame card names something a reader can check.
The other pile is opinion, so it stays off.
Now take the frame pile only.
Match each card to the box it belongs in.
The four boxes are moment, craft choice, effect and who for.
Every card gets a match, even when you are not sure.
A guess I can see beats a blank card.

Key for adjudicating. Goes on the frame: the tall grey print line, the ink line, the eye line, the standing close line. Stays off: it was a really good one, and I liked the artist a lot. Matches: the tall grey print is the moment, the ink is the craft choice, the eye is the effect, standing close is who for.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Fill the half row on the board in front of the group and leave the craft choice box visibly empty. The gap has to be seen, not only described.

blocks.text: A full row beats a half row
Now watch the same moment captured badly.
I write the moment and the effect.
I leave the craft choice box blank.
The row now says the print made me sad.
Nobody can check that against the work.
The craft choice is the box that points.
It names the thing the maker did.

blocks.caption: Same moment, and only one row can be reviewed later
blocks.title: Full row against half row
blocks.alt: Two boxes side by side, the right one drawn with a broken outline, each with an arrow dropping below it

blocks.text: Part B asks for quality and creative impact.
Quality sits in the craft choice box.
Impact sits in the effect box.
Drop one box and half the part is gone.
The last box is who the work was for.
You read that off the work, never off a person.
A print hung low was made for somebody small.
A loud sound was made for a big room.

items: 2 · fill in the craft choice you can point at.
3 · fill in the effect it had on you.
4 · fill in who the work was made for.

blocks.text: A row with a blank box is not finished.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair by table, not by choice. Call ninety seconds out loud, then call the swap.

blocks.text: Fill one row against the clock
Work in twos, with one pack card between you.
Partner one fills a row out loud.
You get ninety seconds, and no longer.
Partner two checks the row with two questions.
Question one is: what can I point at?
Question two is: what did it do to you?
If a box is still empty, say which one.
Then partner one fills it and stops.
Swap over, with two minutes each way.
You may not use nice, weird or boring.
If you stall, name a colour or a sound first.
Speed is the point. Rows get filled while things move.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Scribe for any pupil who asks, and copy their words exactly. Do not upgrade a short row into a better sentence.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil turns a row onto home, family, faith or how somebody looks, say: give me the craft choice and what it did instead. Then write down what they say.

blocks.text: Four rows, captured as it runs
Now work on your own.
Fill four rows on your frame sheet.
One row is one moment. Do not merge two.
Fill all four boxes before you move on.
Mark each row start, middle or end.
Write in pencil, so a box can be changed.
The work may be in the room with you.
It may be on a screen, live or online.
Your four rows are the same either way.
If the work moves or sounds, write while it runs.
If it stays still, look twice and then write.
Then ring the row you would use in a review.
A strong ring holds a craft choice and an effect.
A weak ring holds only a feeling.

items: Supported · fill two rows, each with a craft choice and an effect.
Standard · fill four rows, mark each one start, middle or end, and ring the strongest.
Stretch · as Standard, and write one line saying why that row is the strongest.

blocks.text: If you finish early, add a fifth row from another moment.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult writes the pupil's words, not a tidier version, then adds initials and the date in front of them.

blocks.text: Say one row to an adult
Read your ringed row to the adult at your table.
They write it on your sheet in your words.
Then they add their initials and today's date.
That adult is your audience for this row.
Their initials turn your words into evidence.
A share nobody wrote down is not a share.
The sheet goes in your Part B folder.
Write the file name and the page number on it.
These rows become the review you write next.
Now pick one thing that happens next. Keep the four rows, add a fifth, or change the row you ringed.
Write your pick under the date.

The register refuses in arts log as an evidence locator: it wants the file name plus the page, slide or timecode. Check the file name and page number are on the sheet before it leaves the room, or this row cannot be located at moderation.

print.intro: Fill one row for each moment on this sheet, taking the four boxes in order and marking the row start, middle or end.
focusRows: One moment in each row, with all four boxes filled before the next row starts
A craft choice a reader could point at, and the effect it had, in the pupil's own words
Each row marked start, middle or end, with one row ringed
tiers: Fill two rows, each with a craft choice you can point at and what it did.
Fill four rows with all four boxes, mark each one start, middle or end, and ring the strongest.
As Standard, and write one sentence saying why that row is the strongest.
checks: Each row holds one moment only, with none of the four boxes left blank.
Each craft choice names something a reader could point at in the work.
Each row is marked start, middle or end in its corner.
One row is ringed and carries an adult's initials, today's date and the file name.
